Er, I want to talk about a mistake what I did in my first year in the university.
In our system every semester you must choose your lessons from the internet.
I readed the date in the announcement but I didn't wrote it anywhere, I trusted my memory.
That week I was very busy with a project and I forgot completely this thing.
When I opened the system in Monday morning the page was closed and my lessons was not saved.
I go immediately to the department and I asked to the secretary.
She said me that the system is same for everybody and she cannot do nothing.
So in that semester I taked a lesson about statistics that I really didn't want.
After this I bought a small calendar and now I write all the dates in it.
If the same thing happens today, I will check the deadline two or three times.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: What the mistake was, when it happened, what was done and what would be done today come in sequence, but each point closes in one sentence. Transitions follow the pattern "So", "After this", "If", and the number of sentences given to each section never grows.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary describing enrolment and the deadline is very narrow: date, system, lesson, week repeat, and "lesson" is used in the sense of course (course does not come up). A pattern describing the mistake ("I got it wrong", "put it right") is entirely absent.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: An irregular verb (readed, taked), the form after an auxiliary (didn't wrote), a relative pronoun (a mistake what), adverb placement (forgot completely this thing), preposition (in Monday morning, asked to the secretary), agreement (my lessons was) and a double negative (cannot do nothing) errors are in most sentences; meaning still stands.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Open up the conversation in the department — what was said to the secretary, what the reply was — because that is the response's turning point and it ends in two sentences. In the language, first fix the irregular verbs (read / took) and the form "didn't wrote".

answers.transcript:
So the mistake I want to talk about happened in my first year at university, and honestly it was my fault.
In our system, at the beginning of every semester, you choose your courses online, and the system stays open for one week.
I read the date on the department website, but I didn't write it down, I just trusted my memory.
And that week I was extremely busy with a group project, we were staying in the library until midnight, so it went out of my mind.
When I opened the system on Monday morning, the page was already closed and none of my courses were saved.
I went to the department and I explained to the secretary the situation, but she said the rule is the same for everybody.
So in that semester I had to take a statistics course I didn't want, only because it had free places.
It was not a disaster, I passed it with a good mark, but I lost the elective that I was planning since one year.
After that I bought a small paper calendar, and now I write every deadline in it.
If the same situation happens now, I would put an alarm on my phone one week before.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are developed; last week at the library, Monday morning and the conversation in the department stand as separate scenes and the narrative proceeds through them. The flow becomes mechanical: sections open in the same pattern with "So", "And that week", "When I opened", "After that".
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is vocabulary to carry the topic (trusted my memory, elective, deadline, free places), and meaning is never closed off. Choice slips in two places: "it went out of my mind", "I passed it with a good mark".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A relative clause, the past continuous, obligation (I had to take) and "none of my courses were saved" are controlled; more than two-thirds of sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are specific: word order (I explained to the secretary the situation), the duration structure (I was planning since one year), mixed tense in a conditional clause (If the same situation happens now, I would put).

answers.what_would_lift_it: Make the section on what would be done today concrete: "put an alarm on my phone" is good but stays in a single sentence, even though it is the response's outcome. In the language, fixing "I had been planning for a year" and the tense of the conditional clause is enough.

answers.transcript:
Okay, so the mistake. This was my first year at university, and it was entirely self-inflicted.
The way it works is that at the start of each semester there's a one-week window to pick your courses online, and once it shuts, that's that.
I saw the date on the department website. I remember reading it. And then I didn't write it down, because obviously I'd remember, wouldn't I.
That week we were flat out on a group project, in the library till midnight most nights, and it went clean out of my head.
So I logged on on the Monday morning, all organised, and it had closed at midnight.
I went down to the department and made my case to the secretary, who was very nice about it and completely unmovable, which, fair enough, the rule's the same for everyone.
The upshot was a semester of statistics I had no interest in, purely because it was the only thing left.
It wasn't the end of the world. I did quite well in it, oddly enough. But I lost an elective I'd been looking forward to for the best part of a year.
What I'd do differently is embarrassingly simple. Write it down. I keep a paper diary now, and anything with a deadline goes in it the day I hear about it.
A lesson learnt the hard way, I suppose, and the annoying part is it cost me a semester to learn something my mother had been telling me for years.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative builds its own rhythm: short sentences give the feeling of the mistake's inevitability ("I saw the date on the department website. I remember reading it."), and the closing turns the narrative back on itself by tying the lesson to the mother. There is one interjection ("which, fair enough, the rule's the same for everyone").
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are plentiful and accurate: entirely self-inflicted, once it shuts that's that, flat out, went clean out of my head, made my case, completely unmovable, the upshot was, the end of the world, for the best part of a year, a lesson learnt the hard way.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is wide: the past perfect (it had closed at midnight, I'd been looking forward to), a tag question with "because obviously I'd remember, wouldn't I", a cleft sentence with "What I'd do differently is", an elliptical imperative (Write it down). There is no countable error.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target; for the next level up, whether the paper diary actually works needs to be stated with an example; at present the system is described but its outcome is not given. There is nothing left to do in the language.
